author: sonnet
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Added a short 'how the existing system works' section so a reader new to the stack knows the replica, keyset paging, queue retry semantics and multipart storage rules.
Rewrote every step in the same structure (what starts it, what data moves, where state is kept, what happens on failure), as the brief asked.
Made the vague steps concrete: the table columns, the partial unique index for one-at-a-time, the endpoint behavior, payload contents, job key, buffer and page sizes.
Explained how the memory limit is met (one page plus one buffer, parts of about 8 MB) and checked the 10,000-part limit.
Split the old step 7 and step 8 into the click (duplicate handling), the job (abort on error) and final failure, so each failure case has an owner.
Added at-least-once handling: skip if done and emailed, and resend only the email if the file finished but the email failed, using an emailed_at column.
Stated that the new table lives in the primary database and status reads go to the primary, while row data comes only from the replica.
Explained that an uncompleted multipart upload is invisible, so a half-written file is never downloadable, and that timeouts or dead workers rely on the 24-hour discard rule.
Flagged the 30-minute timeout as a risk with a concrete staging test on the 2-million-row report.
Added an Open points section for orphaned queued rows, expired downloads and nightly rebuilds, instead of hiding those decisions.
Added a one-paragraph summary at the top so the reader knows the overall shape first
Retitled the background section and added row_count, permission and size facts there, so the plan does not assume prior knowledge
Replaced 'the handler' in step 3 with 'the API request handler' to avoid confusion with the job handler
Numbered the 'Building the file' steps and made the 'skip to step 5.7' reference point to 'build step 7'
Noted that a retry that sends only the email creates a fresh 24-hour link
Step 6 now checks for an already-done export so a finished file is not marked failed when only the email failed
Step 8 now says the lifecycle rule, not the plan, does the cleanup
Expired downloads open point now states that the page offers no download link at all
Tightened wording and made 'Starts it / Data moves / State / If it fails' phrasing more uniform

Added an opening check in step 5 that returns immediately if the export is already failed (late duplicate delivery after final failure), and renumbered the checks and the 'skip to build step 7' references.
Changed 'a few tens of MB' wording and minor phrasing for clarity; reworded 'the 500 the page uses' to 'the page's 500'.
Reformatted the Background bullets for the row-reading, job-queue and storage items into nested bullets for easier scanning.
Made 'Building the file' and 'Timeout risk' read as clearly separate labelled parts of step 5 (a period instead of a colon, and Timeout risk now a labelled bullet).
Clarified in step 2 that the size threshold is defined on the unfiltered row_count, so the check is consistent even for filtered exports.
